newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CABINET APPROVES POINTS FOR FARMLAND SALE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CABINET APPROVES POINTS FOR FARMLAND SALE.

text.p: The Czech cabinet has approved the basic conditions of a draft law on the sale of state farmland forests, Agriculture Minister Josef Lux told a news conference on Wednesday.
"We want to privatise the state farmland in the volume of about 500 thousand hectares," he said.
He said that the sale would only be made to Czech citizens or companies, and that forest land would be sold only if it connects plots of farmland as part of the deal.
The land would be sold for the market price on the day determined for each sale, and buyers would be able to pay an instalment system for a period of up to 25-30 years.
The state currently holds a total of 800 thousand hectares of farmland. The remaining 300 thousand hectares not intended for privatisation, would be used for restitution, Lux said.

Before these intial principles can be turned into an act, the government has to approve the draft-law, which then would have to go through three readings in the parliament, a vote in the Senate and a final approval from the president.
The ministry does not expect an actual law on the land sale to take effect before July 1997, Lux's spokeswoman Marcela Dvorakova told Reuters.
